summary: After generation, these 28 claims were checked again outside the agent, either by fetching the provider's page directly on 3 November 2026 or by attempting the step in a real account. 19 held up, 4 were corrected, and 5 could not be verified. They are the claims a developer or the recommendation would rely on. This is a sample, and most claims in the 24 guides were not rechecked.

entries.claim: New apps get one Development Mode Client ID per developer
entries.note: The agent relied on the February 2026 post and missed a July 2026 update that raised the limit to 25 Client IDs sharing one quota. Fixed in the guide, and the agent now has to look for newer changelogs.

entries.claim: The six-week review figure was labelled uncertain, because the agent couldn't read the page
entries.note: The quota modes page states it directly: review can take up to six weeks. Relabelled as sourced.

entries.claim: Extended Quota needs a registered business and at least 250k monthly active users
entries.note: Stated on the quota modes page.

entries.claim: Development Mode requires Premium and allows up to five authorized users per Client ID
entries.note: Stated in Spotify's February 2026 post.

entries.claim: Marketplace review: up to 10 business days, then up to 10 weeks for new submissions, after 10 active workspace installs
entries.note: All three figures are in the review guide.

entries.claim: Non-Marketplace apps are limited to 1 request a minute and 15 objects on conversations.history
entries.note: Stated in Slack's May 2025 changelog entry.

entries.claim: Plans allow 5, 50, 1,000 and 10,000 connections at no charge, $35, $245 and $1,445 AUD a month
entries.note: Matches the pricing table.

entries.claim: Testing mode allows up to 100 test users, and their authorizations expire after seven days
entries.note: Stated in Google's OAuth app audience help page.

entries.claim: Restricted scopes need an annual third-party security assessment, and verification can take several weeks
entries.note: Stated by Google. Google gives no exact range, so the guide's 2-8 weeks is an estimate and stays labelled uncertain.

entries.claim: Marketplace submissions get a reply within 5-10 business days
entries.note: Stated in the listing FAQ.

entries.claim: The distribution method can't be changed once selected
entries.note: Stated on the distribution page.

entries.claim: Repeated review failures can pause an app in a cooldown
entries.note: Stated on the review submission page.

entries.claim: App Store review takes about 2-5 weeks
entries.note: The review page publishes no turnaround time, so this rests on developer forum reports and stays labelled uncertain.

entries.claim: Most logged-in setup flows and all real approval outcomes
entries.note: No app was submitted for review, and no provider approval was attempted. Only GitHub had a test app registered, and it was not connected to Composio. Other steps come from documentation, and live probes only show what an anonymous visitor sees.

entries.claim: The form asks for one Authorization callback URL
entries.note: The real form has Redirect URIs, up to 10, with optional wildcard matching. Expire user access tokens is ticked by default. The guide is fixed. It came from docs that no longer match the page.

entries.claim: Choose From scratch or From a manifest
entries.note: The real dialog offers AI agent, Starter app, From a manifest and Blank app. The guide is fixed.

entries.claim: OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners
entries.note: Stated in the API integration docs.

entries.claim: App Store review has a completeness check of 1-2 business days and a technical review of 3-5
entries.note: Stated on the publishing page.

entries.claim: Full access needs 500 Marketing API calls in the past 15 days
entries.note: Stated in Meta's Marketing API docs.

entries.claim: Webflow aims to decide on a submission within 10 business days
entries.note: Stated in the submission docs.

entries.claim: A private app can be shared with any company through a direct, unlisted link
entries.note: Stated in the private app docs.

entries.claim: The OAuth client is created with CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION inside an account
entries.note: Stated in Snowflake's docs.

entries.claim: Unreviewed apps can be installed, with a warning
entries.note: Klaviyo's docs describe an OAuth installation warning until review.

entries.claim: The X API uses prepaid pay-per-usage credits
entries.note: Stated on the pricing page.

entries.claim: All applications start in the Development tier
entries.note: Stated in Microsoft's LinkedIn docs.

entries.claim: Each customer registers the client in their own tenant
entries.note: Only found in a third party's documentation, not Workday's own.

entries.claim: Public posting needs a separate Content Posting audit
entries.note: The cited source is a third-party blog. TikTok's own docs were not checked here.

entries.claim: Clients are registered per instance in the Application Registry
entries.note: ServiceNow's docs need JavaScript, so this check could not read them.
